title: Wave: Offloading Resource Management to SmartNIC Cores
problem: Userspace system software tasks (kernel thread scheduling, memory management, RPC stacks) consume scarce host CPU cores in cloud servers, reducing the compute available to paying tenants. Existing SmartNIC offload frameworks require custom APIs and cannot handle microsecond-scale system software latencies without host CPU involvement.
motivation: Datacenter operators are under pressure to maximize the fraction of server CPU cycles available to tenants; SmartNICs with ARM cores are now widely deployed but underutilized for host system software offload due to latency and API mismatch.
method: Wave moves system management programs (the code handling task scheduling, memory management, and program-to-program messaging) from the main server CPU to a SmartNIC—a network card with built-in ARM processors. These programs need to respond in microseconds (millionths of a second), so Wave provides a new communication channel between server and SmartNIC that's fast enough to support time-critical decisions. The framework runs existing Linux programs mostly unchanged and without requiring kernel modifications, making the approach practical.
key_novelty: Wave's core innovation is a microsecond-speed communication link that enables system management tasks—task scheduling, memory allocation, and program-to-program messaging—to run on the SmartNIC's ARM processors without extensive code rewrites.
contributions: Wave framework architecture enabling execution of preexisting userspace system software on SmartNIC ARM cores.
New host-SmartNIC communication API supporting us-scale system software offload.
Offload case studies: kernel thread scheduling (saving 16 host cores for memory management), RPCs (saving 8 host cores), and VM management (11.2% performance improvement).
Empirical measurement of performance overhead (1.1%-7.4%) vs. on-host implementations in apples-to-apples comparison.

metrics.other: Saves 16 host cores (memory management), 8 host cores (RPC); 1.1%-7.4% perf overhead vs on-host

limitations: Performance degradation of 1.1%-7.4% vs. on-host implementations makes it unsuitable for the most latency-critical system software paths.
primary_theme: SmartNIC offload of userspace system software
